signal_or_failure: Sales commenced: 'commenced offering products for sale on its Web site in July 1995'
what_it_demonstrated: A live, paying, outside channel existed inside Stage 1, audited after the fact
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Any settled transaction or the day: 'no sales through July 1995' is internally ambiguous (U.1)
notes: Four-way company record (S-1, S-1/A, NYT 1999-03-14, aboutamazon). '16 July' has no primary support.

signal_or_failure: Company press release: books shipped to all 50 states and more than 45 countries 'in just its first four weeks of operation'
what_it_demonstrated: That reach was claimed as possible by the seller, on a dated public record
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Anything independent: this is a company self-report, not verified demand; and it implies counted trading from ~early September, against the filed July date
confidence: High as claim / Low as fact
notes: U.1; U.16. Nine claims in one document are ONE source.

signal_or_failure: Average daily visits ~2,200, explicitly 'not hits'
what_it_demonstrated: A measurable audience existed and the company counted it in the way it chose to file
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Conversion, orders, revenue per visit, or any absolute scale: 2,200 a day is a small number, and no 1995 order count exists
notes: The only 1995 traffic figure ever filed; December 1995 monthly average.

signal_or_failure: Net sales FY1995 (audited)
what_it_demonstrated: Strangers, including foreign ones, paid real money through the site in the first trading year
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Viability: net loss $(303,000) on the same statements; cash existed only because $1,272,000 of equity arrived. Basis: shipment, including outbound shipping and handling, NOT GMV or orders
notes: ~5.5 months of trading: never annualise, never compare with FY1996 (U.9).

signal_or_failure: International sales FY1995
what_it_demonstrated: Demand arrived across borders without any foreign office, currency tooling or translated site
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: No country above 10% of sales is disclosed; the mix of countries is UNKNOWN
notes: MD&A wording 'approximately 39%' is an internal cross-check of the same number, not a second source.

signal_or_failure: Eleven employees
what_it_demonstrated: An organisation existed and could run a search-led storefront
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Capacity: eleven people against an advertised catalogue of >1,000,000 titles; contractors are unquantified
notes: COR-12 supersedes COR-03 (2026-09-23): the count is filed at 1995-12-31 in S-1/A No. 3/No. 5 (S0802/S0803 — 'From December 31, 1995 to March 31, 1997, the Company expanded from 11 to 256 employees'); the original S-1 (S0801) states the same 11 with a 1996-01-01 anchor, which corroborates the population rather than displacing the date. Form 10-K405 discloses no 1995 headcount. 151 (1996-12-31) and 256 (1997-03-31) are post-boundary counts on different dates and are barred from Stage 1.

signal_or_failure: A journalist's search test on the live site returned a little-known Steinbeck title 'within seconds'
what_it_demonstrated: That the search claim was externally testable in-window
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: A delivered order, a payment, or satisfaction: the earliest robust outside evidence of a COMPLETED repeat order is 1996-05-16
notes: Print original not held; reaches us via a 2019 aggregator (RD-011).

signal_or_failure: Placement in Netscape's 'What's New' and Yahoo's 'What's Cool'
what_it_demonstrated: That a two-person firm could earn editorial distribution inside its first quarter of trading
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Order effect, duration, or independence: no dated third-party listing for amazon.com survives; the NCSA Mosaic August-1995 archive lists the river, not the company
notes: U.16. Self-report about the firm's own performance; see channels.csv.

signal_or_failure: Domain amazon.com registered
what_it_demonstrated: About eight months of identity work preceded any recorded sale
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That the company held it (registrant unverifiable) or when the name was adopted
notes: Pre-1996 .com created dates can reflect later record migration.

signal_or_failure: First technical hire, Shel Kaphan, as VP Research and Development
what_it_demonstrated: The build had real engineering capacity nine months before any recorded sale
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That he was a co-founder in law: the filed record is sole-shareholder-founded
notes: ISO effective 1994-10-24 (T01): the first hire predates all outside money.

signal_or_failure: Seafirst Bank merchant account opened under a personal guarantee
what_it_demonstrated: The payment rail could be obtained before there was a balance sheet
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Scale or durability of the rail: amounts, caps and merchant rate are UNKNOWN
notes: Roughly eight months pre-launch; the guarantee stood in for a credit file.

signal_or_failure: First priced outside money at $0.1717 per share
what_it_demonstrated: Outside cash could be raised at a stated price against the founder's plan
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: A valuation: no 1995 whole-company value appears in any document
notes: Also the 1994 option-plan floor strike.

signal_or_failure: S-election terminated with stockholder consent; $107,000 of cumulative losses reclassified to common
what_it_demonstrated: A tax and accounting structure capable of holding outside investors was in place before the round
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That the conversion was planned as a step: no reason is stated in the filing
notes: From April 1995 the burn sits inside the company rather than in the founder's personal return.

signal_or_failure: Wells Fargo bankcard merchant account begins; mother's trust buys 847,716 shares in the same month
what_it_demonstrated: Payment capability widened as trading opened, and family money was priced at the same $0.1717
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Any independent assessment of the business: the priced buyers are father and mother's trust

signal_or_failure: Non-family outside money: Tom A. Alberg signs a shareholder's agreement and buys 150,000 shares at ~$0.3333
what_it_demonstrated: An experienced outside investor committed capital inside Stage 1 at a price roughly double February's
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: A market test of the business: the board seat follows only in June 1996 (post-boundary)
notes: Ex. 10.16 dated 1995-11-26; Certain Transactions and Item 5.

signal_or_failure: Cash $996,000 against $0 of borrowings and $0 long-term obligations
what_it_demonstrated: The first trading year ended funded, without debt
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Independence: the cash is the arrival of $1,272,000 of equity cash, not operating generation (operations consumed $284,000)
notes: The audited cash bridge ties to the dollar: 52 - 232 - 52 + 1,228 = 996.

signal_or_failure: Audited financial statements exist (Ernst & Young) covering 1994-95
what_it_demonstrated: The Stage-1 record rests on audited numbers rather than press claims
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Any 1995 monthly or weekly curve: quarterly disclosure starts at Q1-1996
notes: Filed in 1997, so every in-window fact here is a retrospective filing about an in-window state.

signal_or_failure: Gross margin of 19.96% on shipped sales
what_it_demonstrated: A real retail margin existed on the buy-per-order model
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Sufficiency: marketing and sales ran at 39% of net sales, about twice gross profit
notes: Audited basis; nominal 1995 dollars.

signal_or_failure: ~$17,000 of inventory supporting $511,000 of net sales
what_it_demonstrated: The asset-light mechanism functioned at eleven people
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That the advertised selection could be filled: no fill or back-order rate was ever quantified
notes: Inferred from the audited movement; Note 1 warns of prior-year reclassifications.

signal_or_failure: Period press documents ordering by Web, toll-free telephone or fax at $3.00 per order plus $0.95 per book
what_it_demonstrated: The transaction mechanism was externally observable to a 1995 reader
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That customers liked it: no 1995 satisfaction, returns or chargeback figure exists anywhere
notes: Via a 2019 reprint of Knight Ridder copy; print original not held (RD-011).

signal_or_failure: Free 'Eyes & Editors' notification subscription and solicited reader contributions advertised
what_it_demonstrated: A retention mechanism existed in the product from the first public description
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Any engagement or repeat-visit measurement: none was disclosed for 1995
notes: Company self-report; see channels.csv.

signal_or_failure: AMAZON trademark application filed (SN 75008413, Cl. 042)
what_it_demonstrated: The brand was being formalised while the site traded
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That the name was secure: registration issued only 1997-07-15, and the first asserted conflict is B&N's January-1997 letter (post-boundary)
notes: Document: USPTO TSDR SN 75008413, retrieved 2026-09-23; registered as S1504 in sources.csv (the stage-file appendix register T01-T22 has no entry for it).

signal_or_failure: No name, trademark or litigation conflict is establishable in the Stage-1 record
what_it_demonstrated: That the company operated in-window without disclosed legal jeopardy: 'not currently aware of any legal proceedings pending against it' (1997-03-24)
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That none existed: an unasserted objection leaves no trace, and prior marks in other classes could not be enumerated
confidence: High (that the filing says so) / UNKNOWN (underlying reality)
notes: Required wording: 'establishable in the Stage-1 record', never 'never happened'.

signal_or_failure: Sales tax collected only on shipments into Washington, with no reserve or quantified contingency
what_it_demonstrated: A structural cost advantage over physical retailers in 1995
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Legality or durability: other states 'may seek to impose sales tax collection obligations'; the notes' only contingency is the 1997 B&N suit
notes: Absence of a reserve evidences posture, not absence of exposure.

signal_or_failure: POST-BOUNDARY consequence: ~180,000 cumulative accounts, 100+ countries
what_it_demonstrated: Only that the model was still running into 1996
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Nothing about 1995: 'accounts' is not paying customers and no 1995 account count was ever disclosed
notes: stage2-consequence row, kept out of the Stage-1 snapshot by rule 1.

signal_or_failure: POST-BOUNDARY consequence: '>40% of orders came from repeat customers' (a March-1997 statement about 1997 orders)
what_it_demonstrated: That retention eventually existed
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That Stage-1 demand repeated: 60% (May-1996), 44% (Jan-1997) and >40% (1997) are inconsistent company figures on unpublished definitions
notes: stage2-consequence. See failures.csv: no 1995 repeat-purchase evidence exists.

signal_or_failure: POST-BOUNDARY consequence: FY1996 net sales $15,746,000
what_it_demonstrated: Only the boundary's consequence
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: Nothing in-window: it is not a growth rate measurable from Stage-1 primary data because 1995 was a ~5.5-month period
notes: stage2-consequence row per rule 1.

signal_or_failure: Archive status: no in-window homepage or product image exists to validate the product reconstruction
what_it_demonstrated: That the product must be reconstructed from dated documents rather than artifacts
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That nothing was ever crawled at depth: the capable prefix queries returned HTTP 504, a failure and not a null
notes: COR-04/COR-05: the S-1 '[PICTURES ...]' lines are printer's art instructions; the earliest rendered capture is 1999-08-28.

signal_or_failure: Order counts, average order value and unit economics cannot be measured at all
what_it_demonstrated: Nothing
what_it_did_not_demonstrate: That the business worked or failed per order: the audited ratios make a profitable Stage-1 order structurally implausible, but no order denominator exists to test it
notes: The absence is itself the finding: quarterly disclosure begins only at Q1-1996.
